Base probability on evidence of progress toward the problems on or before this date. These six problems are very difficult, and the difficulty seems intractable.
+ Are problems like these really solvable? Pretty sure, for the prize problems. People have shown their own solutions before.
* Topics for formalization? Predictive AI systems seemed mostly done when I first made my forecast, so unlikely there exists a new topic general enough to qualify.
* What topics are needed in the future? LLMs are straight-forward generalizations of past statistical and signal processing methods so unlikely form sufficiently new topics. Few useful technical contributions have resulted from generative AI so unlikely form matching mitigations.
* How hard will formal systems verification become? Metamath stated that first order theorem provers are very hard for humans to use in 1996 when he first made his forecast, so I have standing to believe it is still very hard.
* How weak is the current state of the art? It's rock bottom as far as we can predict; Nim and Chess classical problem sets are the best available training sets, which are concerning for relevance. Modifications have modest improvements, which it seems is all metastate can do. Formalization is not very developed by 2025, and metternich has not yet released a stand-alone modified SA-FT system for general scheduling problem sets.
* How difficult are solutions to these problems? As far as I can tell the problems are very difficult and intractable, without a way to tackle them that has been discovered yet. I may be missing something.
* When will a solution occur? It seems very unlikely to have much modern progress in 2025, as there seems to be no simple way to reason about math most likely to be relevant to the six problems that seems useful for the question.
* When will solutions appear? Before 26? Reasonable and hopeful analysis has not come to fruition. Non-technological world events? Global climates for flowering subjects. Malignant sequences for AI control. Three years seems too soon to expect a solution. Born in 1987, give up trying to predict.
* When will correction be made? I would not be able to make the conclusion about broken methods and sequences until 2044. Stronger tools for autodidactism are needed since errors seem endemic and the note gives up other good direction; models of math progression of students with halfway reasonable inference to train on. Born in 1976, give up trying to fix the increasing lack of guidance and support.
* When will the next update be correct? I am unlikely to have the time to judge results another 8 years; problem analysis ofin my old come to an end before hand. There should be either more specific technical tools, or better technical resources with some more significant LLM support early in 2044. No snow fight Today. Environmental data that does not exist. Combined with academic statistics about it. Until only after about 9 years with many events in between. Today. Will all rewrite the trigonometry of the world.

formatted_prompt:
Forecast date: 2025-04-29. Make a forecast from this date. Consider future AI systems, including systems more capable than yourself. Use your existing knowledge.

Forecast target: At least one of the six Millennium Prize Problems that were open at the forecast date: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture, Hodge conjecture, Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness, P versus NP, Riemann hypothesis, or Yang-Mills existence and mass gap. Poincaré is excluded because it was already solved at the forecast date.

Forecast event: a correct complete solution to at least one of these problems, meeting its original Clay Mathematics Institute mathematical formulation, is first publicly available, and AI has contributed an identifiable new mathematical argument or proof step incorporated into that solution. Substantive human-AI collaboration qualifies. Correctness may be established by later validation; a Clay prize need not be awarded by the deadline. Partial progress alone does not qualify. Give one probability for at least one qualifying solution by each deadline; do not give separate probabilities for individual problems.

Assign a probability to the event occurring on or before each of the listed deadlines. The deadlines are December 31 of 2026, 2030, 2035, 2040, and 2050. Probabilities must be numbers between 0 and 1 inclusive, nondecreasing with the deadline. Account for the possibility the event never occurs. Give your own best probability estimates despite uncertainty. Return only one JSON object with exactly the keys "2026", "2030", "2035", "2040", and "2050" and their numerical probabilities, with no markdown or explanation.
